rics.meaning: Money Supply M1 (method break Jan 2011) — narrow money level. Methodology revised in 2011 to align with international standards.
rics.how_to_use: Pre/post-2011 series not directly comparable due to methodology break. Use post-2011 data for trend analysis. M1 = currency in circulation + demand deposits at banks.

rics.meaning: Money Supply M2 — broad money level published by Bank Indonesia. Includes M1 (currency + demand deposits) plus quasi-money (time deposits, savings deposits, foreign currency deposits at banks).
rics.how_to_use: Track YoY growth (aIDM2AR) for cyclical signal. Foreign currency deposit share — when it rises sharply, indicates IDR mistrust (dollarization). Recent share ~15-18% of M2; spikes during IDR weakness episodes.

rics.meaning: Money Supply M2, YoY change — alternative release of broad money growth rate.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDCMS2YB/A. The headline M2 growth gauge for monetary-policy analysis.

rics.meaning: Money Supply Currency — currency in circulation outside the banking system. Subset of M1.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks public's cash demand. Indonesia is still cash-heavy (digital payment adoption growing rapidly post-2020). Lebaran-Eid drives the largest annual cash spike.

rics.meaning: Money Supply M0 (Monetary Base) — currency in circulation plus banks' reserve deposits at Bank Indonesia. Direct BI liability that expands with reserve creation.
rics.how_to_use: Distinct from M1/M2 — captures BI balance-sheet expansion. Useful for tracking unconventional easing periods (2020-22 BI bond purchases). Compare to M2 for the bank-lending multiplier (currently ~6x).

rics.description: Money Supply M0, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Money Supply M0, month-over-month change — high-frequency monetary-base pulse.
rics.how_to_use: Volatile. Smooth with 3-month average for trend. Spikes around Lebaran-Eid as currency demand surges (cash withdrawals for holiday).

rics.description: Money Supply M0, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Money Supply M0, year-over-year change — pace of monetary base expansion.
rics.how_to_use: M0 growth signals BI's stance. Surges 2020-22 reflected COVID-era unconventional easing (burden-sharing with Treasury). Track for unconventional policy signals.

rics.meaning: Money Supply M1 (Standardized) — narrow money level (currency + demand deposits). Most-liquid money aggregate.
rics.how_to_use: Use level for analytical baseline; YoY (aIDCMS1YB/A) for cyclical signal. M1 leads economic activity by 2-4 months.

rics.description: Money Supply M1, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Money Supply M1, MoM percent change — high-frequency narrow-money pulse.
rics.how_to_use: Volatile (Lebaran cash demand drives big swings). Smooth with 3-month average. Use YoY for trend.

rics.description: Money Supply M1, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Money Supply M1, year-over-year change — narrow money (currency in circulation + demand deposits at banks). The most-liquid money aggregate.
rics.how_to_use: M1 growth leads economic activity by 2-4 months because it captures transaction demand. M1 acceleration ahead of GDP suggests upcoming activity pickup. Pair with M2 — divergence (M1 up, M2 flat) signals shift from time deposits to demand (lower interest rates, weaker savings incentive).

rics.description: Money Supply M2, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Money Supply M2, month-over-month change — high-frequency broad-money pulse.
rics.how_to_use: Volatile. Smooth with 3-month average. Sustained MoM contraction (rare) signals tight liquidity.

rics.description: Money Supply M2, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Money Supply M2, year-over-year change — broad money including currency, demand deposits, time/savings deposits, and money market mutual funds. The headline Indonesia liquidity gauge published monthly by Bank Indonesia.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia M2 typically grows 6-10% YoY in normal cycles. Sustained sub-5% signals tight liquidity (often during BI hike cycles); >12% suggests aggressive easing or external inflows (commodity boom). Pair with credit growth — when M2 rises faster than credit, banks are accumulating liquid assets (gov bonds) rather than lending.

rics.meaning: Money Supply M2 (Standardized) — broad money level. Companion to aIDM2 in standardized framing.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDM2. Use YoY (aIDCMS2YB/A) for the cyclical signal.
